---
title: "What section is the model actually analysing?"
---

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
c = 0.05  # the baseline root chord, where the stock is a 10% slab
drawn = flat_plate(c, bevel=BEVEL)
analysed = drawn.to_kulfan_airfoil()

x = np.linspace(0, 1, 401)
t_drawn, t_analysed = drawn.local_thickness(x), analysed.local_thickness(x)
tc_drawn, tc_analysed = np.max(t_drawn), np.max(t_analysed)
te_gap_mm = float(analysed.local_thickness(1.0)) * c * 1e3

# The two representations must return the SAME polar -- that is the claim the
# entry rests on, and it is what shows the fit was already in the path.
a = np.linspace(0, 8, 9)
pd = drawn.get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a, Re=1.5e4, mach=0.0)
pa = analysed.get_aero_from_neuralfoil(alpha=a, Re=1.5e4, mach=0.0)
assert np.all(pd["CD"] == pa["CD"]) and np.all(pd["CL"] == pa["CL"])
assert tc_analysed > tc_drawn and te_gap_mm > 0
```

::: {.hero-pair}
::: {.hero-ref}
[`{python} f"{tc_drawn:.1%}"`]{.hero-value}
[thickness ratio, as drawn]{.hero-label}
:::
::: {}
[`{python} f"{tc_analysed:.1%}"`]{.hero-value}
[thickness ratio, as analysed]{.hero-label}
:::
:::

**Answer.** A Kulfan (CST) fit of the plate, never the plate itself —
`get_aero_from_neuralfoil` performs that fit internally, so the two
representations return bit-identical polars (@fig-section). The fit rounds what a
razor cannot: peak thickness gains [`{python} f"{tc_analysed - tc_drawn:.1%}"`]{.key}
of chord, the trailing edge fails to close by
[`{python} f"{te_gap_mm:.2f}"` mm]{.key}, and the bevel is smeared. Every
coefficient in this chapter already carried this.

::: {.callout-warning}
## The bevel is the casualty
Any conclusion about edge treatment rests on a shape that cannot fully resolve an edge.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Assumed

1. **Reynolds number: 15 000**, mid-range for this chapter.
2. **Chord: `{python} f"{c * 1e3:.0f}"` mm**, the baseline root chord.
:::

```{python}
#| label: fig-section
#| fig-cap: "Half-thickness of the drawn plate and of the CST fit that NeuralFoil is given, at a 50 mm chord. Left, the whole section; right, the leading-edge bevel at ten times the horizontal scale. Vertical scale is exaggerated on both."
fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.0, 2.6))
for ax, xmax in [(ax1, 1.0), (ax2, 0.1)]:
    m = x <= xmax
    ax.plot(x[m], t_drawn[m] / 2, label="as drawn")
    ax.plot(x[m], t_analysed[m] / 2, ls="--", label="as analysed")
    ax.plot(x[m], -t_drawn[m] / 2, color="C0")
    ax.plot(x[m], -t_analysed[m] / 2, ls="--", color="C1")
    ax.set_xlabel("x/c")
    ax.grid()
ax1.set_ylabel("y/c")
ax1.legend(loc="upper right")
ax2.set_title("leading edge", fontsize=9)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
